enumeration.method: Independent font-sensitive enumeration of all 37 main pages finds exactly CMBX10 Theorem headings 1,2,3,4. Theorem 1 continues from page 10 onto page 11. Main references end on page 37; the saved heading crop establishes Appendix A on a separate page 38.

checks: Inventory and final census pass separate validator invocations. The independent inventory hash is unchanged and all original theorem fields survive the handoff.
The four authors, arXiv v2 stamp of 4 July 2023, versioned URL, 111-page count, source hash and main-text endpoint match the pinned source.
All theorem bodies were visually checked on pages 10,11,15,21,30. The full continuation of Theorem 1 and all three parts and optional stronger localization clause of Theorem 2 are retained.

The 39 source passages were inspected against rendered main pages. Numbered Assumptions keep their source type, and natural-language names, naming contexts and all highlight selectors are source-backed.
Theorem 2 imports condition (15) but not the separate log-bandwidth condition of Theorem 1. Its algorithm threshold is an input rather than a mandatory Gaussian critical quantile.

Theorem 3 uses Assumptions 1-3 and 5, the localized null, neighborhood sizes, normalized statistic and its own printed Gaussian covariance. Assumptions 4,6,7 and the spatial consistency Proposition are not added.
Theorem 4 reaches exactly the 16 general-model interfaces D25-D40. Independent assertions exclude all VMA, diagonal-filter and earlier Gaussian-law interfaces from its reach.

The general and linear moment, temporal-dependence and scale conditions remain separate. The covariance free index, missing zero-lag case, coupling domains, random lattice design and variance-versus-standard-deviation conflict are documented without rewriting formulas.

Ten auxiliary source passages resolve norms, asymptotics, section conventions, condition (15), optional calibration, temporal locations, signal sign, product index and bandwidth. Fifteen source notes record remaining interpretation limits.

The final graph has 34 direct theorem uses and 59 deduplicated same-paper connections. Every interface has a source-backed explanation for every related theorem, and all statement evidence stays in the main text with balanced mathematical grouping.

Registered-source revalidation corrected the D5 source wording from long-run covariance matrix to long-run variance matrix, including its name, keyword and highlight phrase; all formulas and theorem statements are unchanged.

source_notes: This is a census of the pinned arXiv v2 preprint; identity with journal wording has not been established.
Complete means source-fidelity and statement-dependency review is complete. It does not certify the paper’s proof correctness or silently resolve ambiguous source formulas.
Appendix bodies are excluded. References to appendix-only variance estimation or detailed covariance calculations are recorded, without importing those constructions.

unresolved_source_references.note: The notation paragraph says a_n>>b_n means a_n/b_n tends to zero. This reverses the conventional reading used by the later signal and threshold discussion. Both the notation and original theorem inequalities are retained without choosing a correction.

The trend adds gamma_k at a break, whereas the local contrast and jump estimate subtract the right mean from the left. At an isolated positive jump their expectation has the opposite sign. Equation (20) nevertheless prints a positive tent-weighted gamma_k, and Theorem 2(iii) compares gamma-hat_k minus gamma_(k*). The disagreement is preserved.
The minimum starts at k=0 but the model only defines gamma_1,...,gamma_K. No gamma_0 convention is supplied. The original index range is not changed to make the condition well formed.

At Q_n=omega the algorithm enters its else branch but its strict-exceedance candidate set is empty, leaving max{k:A_k nonempty} undefined. Argmax and nearest-break ties have no explicit selection rule. Estimated quantities indexed up to true K also need an extension off the high-probability event K-hat=K. These omissions are not filled into source statements.

The jump estimate evaluates the left mean at tau-hat_k-bn and right mean at tau-hat_k+bn-1. These shifted windows can fall outside the observed range for candidate locations allowed by Algorithm 1. No boundary extension rule is supplied. The original shifts and subtraction order are retained.

unresolved_source_references.note: The exact centering in (7) uses coordinate variances at a fixed index. Remark 5 approximates it by 2p/(bn); the discussion after Theorem 2 instead writes an expectation at a selected random index. These expressions are not silently identified. The extracted centering and theorem use the original bar-c definition.

The displayed covariance has an overlap indicator with a free j, and no sum over j. It also invokes Xi from (11), which already includes a factor p. This does not unambiguously define the full comparison covariance. The printed expression is retained without inferring an overlap-count correction.

The numbered definition specifies coordinate subsets, while surrounding prose describes adjacent series and uses contiguity in a window-count argument. The definition itself is retained; an arbitrary set is not silently rewritten as an interval. Assumptions 6-7 and the influenced-set construction belong to Proposition 1, not a stored Theorem.

The source simultaneously puts locations in Z^v and represents them as scaled iid vectors having a density bounded above and away from zero on [0,1]^v. No rounding or alternative ambient space is specified. The density assumption is preserved as written, rather than replaced by the separate mass-to-volume discussion. Independence of random locations from the noise is not explicitly stated.

The source calls each interval an interval on Z and then assigns its rectangle Lebesgue volume. A literal finite lattice rectangle has zero Lebesgue measure; a continuous enclosing rectangle would be a different interpretation. The source does not state that change of interpretation. Its mass comparability condition is retained with the full definition.

Equation (5) uses sigma_j squared for the long-run variance; equation (44) instead defines sigma(l)=sigma(l,l) as the variance, but later inverses and the correlation ratio use sigma(l) as if it were a standard deviation. The general formulas are preserved with no square-root correction. Unlike (5), the general setup does not explicitly repeat a uniform positive variance bound.

The nonlinear representation uses ell-prime in Z^v, but both displayed coupled versions use Z. The replacement rule is stated only for i>=0 although the process uses an entire negative-time history. The double-star rule replaces i=0 OR s=0, not only their intersection. These source domains and logical conditions are retained.

The piecewise covariance formula covers only zeta>0 and does not state its diagonal or other same-time entries. The overlap indicator requires both spatial indices in the intersection of the two rectangles, as printed. No zero-lag limit or different overlap weights are supplied by the census. The detailed evaluation is referred to appendix Lemma 15, which was not read.

Theorems 1 and 3 explicitly exclude dependence of the implicit constant on n,p,b; Theorem 4 additionally excludes S. These exact clauses are retained, as are the different error rates. The Gaussian comparison laws are finite vectors depending on the asymptotic parameters, not a single fixed limiting distribution.

The variance estimator is referred to Appendix A.1 and the detailed general covariance evaluation to Lemma 15 in Appendix C. No appendix body was inspected. The census preserves the known-scale main-text statistic and records the covariance specification omissions rather than importing those details.

ambient_resolution.shared: Basic real vector spaces, finite sums, indicators, expectation, variance, Gaussian laws, suprema, minima, logarithms and convergence notation remain ambient. A1 gives source norm/rate conventions; A2 gives n∧p→∞; A10 gives the common moving-window bandwidth. Every paper-specific object is resolved by the local interfaces or auxiliary passages. Statements and conditions with unresolved source conventions remain original claims, not certified well-posed theorems.
ambient_resolution.1: Assumptions 1,2,3 resolve to D10,D11,D12 under the VMA convention A3. The null is D2, Q_n is D8 and Z_i is D9. Delta_0,Delta_1,Delta_2 and the real supremum variable are bound inline. The additional log-bandwidth and (15) rates are a separate convergence clause. The covariance is the explicit (11)-(12) law; no proof X_j construction or Gaussian critical quantile is needed.
ambient_resolution.2: Assumptions 1-4 resolve to D10,D11,D12,D16. The referenced rate (15) is A4. K and gamma_k come from D1, Lambda from D5, kappa_n and tau_k from D13/A6, delta_p from D14, and all estimated quantities from Algorithm 1 D15; bar-c is D7. Omega is the algorithm input satisfying the displayed rate and signal requirements, with no mandatory use of optional A5. Gamma_k and nearest-break k* are bound inline. All three conclusions and the stronger optional localization condition are preserved; the signal-index, sign and estimator-domain issues are recorded separately.
ambient_resolution.3: Assumptions 1-3 and 5 resolve to D10,D11,D12,D20. D19 supplies the localized no-break model, D22 the normalized Two-Way statistic, D23 its Gaussian comparison vector and D17 the minimum neighborhood size. A8 supplies the finite product index N without creating an extra interface. All Delta terms, the real threshold variable and the two additional convergence conditions are inline. Assumptions 4,6,7, Algorithm 1, Definition 5 and Proposition 1 are not imported.
ambient_resolution.4: Assumptions 8-12 resolve to D28,D29,D36,D37,D38 under the nonlinear spatial model D25,D26,D30. The null is no jumps in (43), as stated in the context of (46). Q-tilde is D35; Z-tilde is D40 with rho-tilde D39; B_min and its comparability convention are D27. N is A8, while v is the fixed spatial dimension D25 and xi is the exponent in Assumption 12. The q parameter comes from Assumptions 10/11. c_(p,n), the three Delta terms, the real supremum variable and both extra convergence rates are bound inline. A9 resolves the shared break-time parameter convention only. No VMA, diagonal independence, linear covariance, positive-signal or localization algorithm assumptions are inherited.

review_limits: Source statements and their prerequisites were reviewed; the original source’s mathematical inconsistencies remain documented.
No appendix body or external supplement was read.
